intro: Greeks speak one of the oldest recorded languages in the world, and the Orthodox Church and family are at the heart of daily life.

chapters.title: People and language
text: About a third of Greeks live in and around Athens; Thessaloniki is the second city. Greek has been written for more than 3,000 years, and the Greek alphabet was the model for the Latin and Cyrillic alphabets.
Millions of people of Greek origin live abroad, especially in the United States and Australia; Melbourne has one of the largest Greek communities outside Greece.

chapters.title: Faith and festivals
text: Most Greeks belong to the Greek Orthodox Church, and Easter is the biggest celebration, with candlelit processions, fireworks at midnight, red-dyed eggs and roast lamb. Many Greeks celebrate their name day more than their birthday.

keyTerms.meaning: The eastern branch of Christianity, followed in Greece, Russia and much of Eastern Europe.
